title: 3160 Manual Transmission: Layout and Identification
introduction:
This overview covers the 3160 manual gearbox. I start with its layout, then use the identification tag to keep the right transmission attached to the right information. “Mustang gearbox” is a family description, not a parts-ordering strategy.

The exterior drawing shows the assembled housings; the tag illustration connects a highlighted location to an enlarged label. Match its callouts to the accompanying table to distinguish part identification from manufacturing information. This is a guide to construction and identification, rather than a removal, diagnosis or fluid-service procedure.

edits.why: The features below explain how the gearbox selects drive and how its major assemblies are arranged.

edits.text: The 3160 6-speed manual transmission combines the following gear-selection, housing and cooling features:
edits.why: Reading these as related systems makes the feature list more useful than a collection of specifications.

edits.text: It provides six forward speeds and one reverse speed.
edits.why: The forward ratios change the relationship between engine rotation and driveline rotation.

edits.text: The forward gears are synchronized and have helical-cut teeth.
edits.why: Synchronizers bring rotating parts toward compatible speeds before engagement; helical describes the angled tooth form.

edits.text: Reverse uses a fully synchronized, constant-mesh gear system.
edits.why: Constant mesh means the gear teeth remain engaged with their mating gears; selecting reverse does not mean sliding those teeth into mesh.

edits.text: A shift interlock prevents more than one gear from being engaged at the same time.
edits.why: The interlock keeps selection exclusive, like a gate that admits only the chosen drive path.

edits.text: The shift forks have removable wear pads.
edits.why: Removable describes their construction; it does not supply an inspection limit or a replacement procedure.

edits.text: The main case, extension housing and clutch housing are aluminum.
edits.why: Use the exterior illustration to recognize the housing sections as parts of the complete assembly.

edits.text: An oil pump inside the clutch housing circulates fluid for cooling.
edits.why: The pump gives fluid cooling a dedicated circulation feature within the gearbox.

edits.text: The transmission multiplies engine torque and carries it from the crankshaft toward the driveshaft connected to the rear differential. Its three-shaft layout is coaxial: the input and output shafts share a single axis. All gear wheels have helical teeth and remain constantly engaged with their mating gears. The maximum design torque is 576 Nm. Roller ball detents and linear shift rail bearings reduce shift effort, while the 3160 uses double and triple cone hybrid and sintered bronze synchronizers on all gears. These synchronizers bring rotating parts toward compatible speeds before the selected gear engages. The transmission fluid is designed for the transmission’s entire service life and does not require changing during servicing.
edits.why: Coaxial describes the shared input/output centerline, rather than saying every shaft occupies that line. The torque figure is a transmission design rating, not a fastener-tightening value. The lifetime-fluid statement describes routine servicing; this overview supplies no filling or repair method.
The enlarged label and its table distinguish the replacement part identifier from assembly and build information. Do not treat every printed code as an interchangeable part number.

edits.text: Locate the transmission identification tag on the top RH side of the transmission, as highlighted in the illustration.
edits.why: RH means right-hand. I match each highlighted label field to the table before interpreting it; the pictured codes are examples, and no physical access procedure or date-code decoding convention is given here.
